name: Oal (Jimikand) Curry
ingredients: 1 tablespoon lemon juice or amchur (dry mango powder)
instructions: 1. Peel and cut the Oal into cubes. Boil them in water with a dash of lemon juice or tamarind to neutralize the calcium oxalate crystals, then drain.
2. Heat mustard oil in a pan and shallow-fry the Oal cubes until golden brown. Remove and set aside.
3. In the same oil, add cumin and mustard seeds. Once they splutter, add the chopped onions and sauté until translucent.
4. Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté for a minute, then stir in the tomato puree, turmeric, chili powder, and salt.
5. Cook the masala until the oil separates from the sides of the pan.
6. Add the fried Oal cubes, mix well to coat with spices, and add water to reach the desired consistency.
7. Simmer for 10 minutes, sprinkle with garam masala, and garnish with fresh coriander before serving.
description: Oal (Jimikand) curry is a staple vegetarian delicacy in Bihar, often referred to as 'Suran' elsewhere. It is traditionally prepared during festive occasions and marriages, known for its unique 'meat-like' texture and rich, spicy mustard-based gravy.
